s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive abdominal pain and distension with a large hepatic mass and vascular complications
salient_findings: Abdominal distension without guarding or rebound
17 × 9 cm mixed solid and cystic mass in the right hepatic lobe
Compression of the inferior vena cava (IVC) and near-occlusive embolus in the left pulmonary artery
key_facts: 8-year-old girl with no significant medical history
1-week history of progressive abdominal pain
Nausea and vomiting
Abdominal distension without guarding or rebound
17 × 9 cm mixed solid and cystic mass in the right hepatic lobe
Compression of the inferior vena cava (IVC)
Percutaneous biopsy of the mass and placement of a drain
Persistent sanguineous output from the drain
Anemia and concern for hemorrhage
Infrarenal IVC thrombus and near-occlusive embolus in the left pulmonary artery
Compression of the distal IVC at its junction with the right atrium

shortlist.label: Hepatoblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large hepatic mass in a child with progressive abdominal pain and distension

shortlist.label: Embryonal sarcoma of the liver
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive hepatic tumor with potential for vascular complications

shortlist.label: Hepatic angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare but possible cause of hepatic mass with hemorrhage and vascular thrombosis

shortlist.label: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant tumor that can present with abdominal pain and distension

shortlist.label: Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma of the liver
shortlist.why_kept: Vascular tumor that can cause hepatic mass and thrombosis

raw.rationale: The patient's age, presentation with a large abdominal mass, and the presence of a mixed solid and cystic mass in the liver are consistent with hepatoblastoma, which is the most common primary liver cancer in children.

rejected.label: Embryonal sarcoma of the liver
rejected.why: While possible, embryonal sarcoma is less common than hepatoblastoma in children and typically presents at an older age.

rejected.label: Hepatic angiosarcoma
rejected.why: This is a rare tumor that is more commonly associated with exposure to toxic substances and is unlikely in a child with no significant medical history.

rejected.label: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma
rejected.why: This diagnosis is less likely given the presence of a distinct mass and the patient's age, which is more consistent with hepatoblastoma.

rejected.label: Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma of the liver
rejected.why: This is a rare tumor that typically presents in adults and is less likely in a child with the described clinical presentation.
